GENIE.AI walkthrough · Public-sector briefing

Whose knowledge shapes an AI answer?

An open-source framework for public services, from the source document to the system that answers the question.

01 / 43
GENIE.AI is an open-source framework for public services, and this walkthrough follows one question — what a citizen needs to bring to renew a permit — from the answer on screen back through the service, the knowledge and the infrastructure that produced it. The framework is aimed at people who need both its public-service value and how it works. The permit, its guide and the instructions that go with it are fictional: they are a thread for explaining the framework, not policy advice. The closing slide leaves time for questions.

The public-service challenge

Local knowledge changes the service.

THE PUBLIC-SERVICE CHALLENGE

What the model already knows

A general model can explain what permit renewal usually means and help write a clear response.

What the institution knows

The local authority knows which form applies, which proof it accepts and who publishes a change.

What the user needs

A reliable answer for this jurisdiction, with enough evidence to check or challenge it.

03 / 43
A fluent, plausible explanation is not the same as an answer that applies to a particular jurisdiction today. A general model can help phrase an answer; the local requirements have to come from the institution's own maintained sources. When the policy changes, the knowledge and its publication process must carry that change into the service. The first design question follows from this: who owns the source, and how does a change reach the users?

Several ways to fit GENIE.AI into an existing ecosystem.

FOUR INTEGRATION POINTS

Your applications

A government portal or staff application calls the assistant API and shows the answer with its sources in its own pages, as the web and mobile apps do.

Your sign-in

Users sign in with the institution's own identity provider. The platform trusts it, and each request carries the user's roles.

Your documents

Existing documents reach the knowledge base through the document APIs or the dashboard: upload, ingestion and search, in the usual office formats.

Your models

The model services can run on the institution's own GPU hosts or behind a dedicated GPU API.

API reference · External identity provider · Document ingestion · GPU tier
08 / 43
Four ways into an existing ecosystem, one per card. An agency portal or staff application calls the assistant API and presents the answer itself; the web and mobile clients are clients of that same API. Users keep the identity they already have: the platform's sign-in service (Keycloak) brokers the institution's provider and issues the token the applications present, and the roles in that token decide what each request may read. Documents already published reach the knowledge base through the document APIs or the dashboard. The model services can run on the institution's own GPU hosts or behind a GPU API it controls. The integrating agency remains responsible for its application logic and for any decision it makes from the response.

11 / 43
A source document has to become searchable before it can answer anything. An authorised user uploads a file; it stays Pending; an administrator triggers Ingest from the dashboard or the API. The configured pipeline scans uploads with ClamAV when enabled, extracts supported formats with the available parser, splits the text into chunks, creates embeddings and stores the searchable result. Docling handles supported formats such as PDF and DOCX in the reference setup. The highlighted overlap is why adjacent chunks can share context: smaller chunks may improve focus but can also cut the context in half, so size and overlap have to be evaluated against real documents. These are deployment settings, not per-question choices. When the chunking or the embedding model changes, the affected files are re-ingested and retrieval is checked again. The sample guide and the chunks are fictional.

How the answer is built

Hybrid retrieval combines meaning and exact wording.

BM25 search

Rank lexical matches, such as a form number or a precise procedure name. GENIE.AI fuses the vector and lexical rankings.

Vector search

Find passages with related meanings, such as “renew my permit” and “extend its validity”.

Graph expansion

Optional graph traversal adds related chunks. Candidate retrieval remains subject to the account’s available knowledge.

Hybrid retrieval · Access control
13 / 43
The renewal question brings two useful signals together. Vector search finds passages with a related meaning even when the wording differs; BM25 surfaces exact terms such as a form name or a procedure number. GENIE.AI combines the lexical and the vector rankings, and optional graph expansion adds linked material. No single signal guarantees a correct answer — the retrieved passages still have to match the request and the user's access.

RAG pipeline · Reranking
14 / 43
Reranking re-orders the candidates the retrieval returned: the renewal passage moves above the passages that mention the same permit but answer a different question. It evaluates a bounded candidate set; it does not recover a passage the retrieval never found, and it can be switched off. The illustration shows an ordering, not a measured quality improvement. A deployment compares the settings on representative questions and reviews the evidence — performance cannot be inferred from the animation.

A Kiswahili question is normalised to English before the retrieval, and the answer comes back in Kiswahili. The flags label the example languages; they do not imply that every language is enabled by default. In this documented path, the supported incoming text is normalised for the English-centred pipeline, while the source documents are prepared in English before standard ingestion — the ordinary ingestion flow does not translate a corpus automatically. Streaming translation is handled by the backend at the response edge, ChatQnA handles the non-streaming path. Names, dates, exceptions and legal or administrative terms need testing with fluent reviewers.

What runs inside GENIE.AI?

AN ITU-INITIATED FRAMEWORK · APACHE 2.0 CODE LICENCE

Web & mobile

Vue 3 powers the web client. Flutter powers the Android and iOS clients.

Application & identity

The Node.js and Express backend brokers requests. Keycloak handles sign-in and identity.

Knowledge

Docling parses documents. ArangoDB stores indexed knowledge, including vector and graph data.

AI services

OPEA ChatQnA orchestrates RAG. TEI serves embeddings and reranking. vLLM serves generation.

Observability

OpenTelemetry collects signals. Victoria stores them. Grafana visualises them when enabled.

Deployment

The application runs on Docker Compose, Docker Swarm or Kubernetes via Helm.

Architecture · Apache 2.0 licence
17 / 43
Each layer has a role. The user interfaces; the application and identity layer, where the Node.js and Express backend brokers the requests and Keycloak handles sign-in; document processing and storage, with Docling parsing and ArangoDB holding the indexed knowledge, vector and graph data; AI orchestration and model services, where OPEA ChatQnA orchestrates the RAG, TEI serves the embeddings and the reranking and vLLM serves the generation; and telemetry, collected by OpenTelemetry, stored by the Victoria components and shown in Grafana when enabled. This is the documented reference stack, not a requirement to activate every optional component in every deployment. Compose, Swarm and Kubernetes also differ in their edge and operational components. The Apache 2.0 licence applies to the framework code; model weights, datasets and third-party services carry their own terms, which the institution must review.

How knowledge is governed

OKF makes curated knowledge versionable.

OPEN KNOWLEDGE FORMAT · CONCEPTS, LINKS AND SERVING GRAPHS

Concepts

Each concept is a Markdown document with YAML frontmatter. It captures a distinct topic such as proof of address.

Relationships

Typed links connect concepts across the knowledge base. A stewardship team can review the content and its links.

Serving graph

Enable OKF and select OKF-only or hybrid retrieval to search published, ingested repositories as separate graphs.

OKF Studio · Access control · OKF configuration
19 / 43
OKF is a structured way to curate concepts and their typed relationships, with the content stored in a versioned repository. Three actions stay distinct: editing a draft, publishing a version, and making the resulting knowledge available for serving after the ingestion. OKF is configurable and can be disabled; the existing free-form corpus remains a separate path. When OKF is enabled, the selected retrieval mode decides whether the queries use the OKF serving graph alone or combine it with the legacy corpus. The benefit is a governed structure and a visible lifecycle, not automatic correctness.

21 / 43
The workflow runs from the draft to the serving: create or import the source material, curate the concepts and their links, inspect the flagged personal data, then test the query routing in the Testing Lab. That test checks the intended repository selection before the publication; it does not prove that the ingested corpus will return the desired passage. The publication creates a version and triggers the ingestion, after which the operators verify the serving status and probe the retrieval. The supporting lifecycle controls — approval, version history, unpublishing and retraction — are the tools for a managed change.

22 / 43
Two assumptions come first: the public guide is unrestricted, the internal procedure sits in a separate restricted repository. In the default open mode, the unrestricted repositories are available and a matching grant can add the restricted one. In closed mode, the regular users need explicit read scopes for the repositories they may search. These settings define the retrieval access; they do not grant editing or publishing rights, which are controlled separately. Each grant needs an owner and a review.

24 / 43
Knowledge ownership is an operating responsibility, and a changed requirement shows why. The policy owner confirms what changed and which source is authoritative; the editor updates the affected sources and their published versions, reviews and publishes the revision; the operations or service team confirms the ingestion and checks the expected answer. The audit history and the ingestion log help investigate what changed and whether the new version is serving. The handoff has to be defined by the institution, not assumed from the software.

27 / 43
Two profiles, two controls. Keycloak establishes the identity and issues the OIDC token; the application validates that identity and uses the configured roles and scopes to decide the access. The application roles govern the functions in GENIE.AI, while the repository read scopes decide which knowledge repositories can be searched. The two are related but not interchangeable. Both the sign-in and the effective retrieval need testing with representative accounts, before the launch and after every access change.
GENIE.AI
Running a trustworthy service

Data protection, level by level.

USERS · OPERATIONS · INFRASTRUCTURE

People’s rights

Each user can delete a conversation. The settings offer a data reset and an account deletion; deleting the account erases the personal data in the profile.

Logs and telemetry

Passwords, tokens, e-mail addresses and the text of questions, answers and documents are masked in the logs as they are collected. The retention of logs, metrics and traces is a deployment setting.

Where the data lives

Files and indexes stay in the institution’s deployment. Model calls go to the GPU or GPU API chosen, which may sit beyond its network.

Connect these levels in the institution’s data protection analysis: the platform provides the mechanisms, the institution makes the assessment.

Account settings · Observability · GPU tier
28 / 43
Three levels, next to the access control of the previous slide. Users act on their own data: a conversation can be deleted from the saved chats — it disappears from the user for good; what the platform keeps beyond it, backups and logs, is a point to confirm with the platform team. The settings page offers a data reset and an account deletion. The account deletion is the mechanism the platform provides for an erasure request: it deletes the Keycloak user and nulls the personal data in the profile. Operations decide what is kept: container logs pass a redaction transform in the collector before they are stored — it works from a fixed list of keys and patterns, and anything outside it, a name or a phone number in free text, is stored as written — and the retention of logs, metrics and traces is set per deployment. Infrastructure decides where the data goes: files and indexes stay in the deployment, while model calls follow the GPU or GPU API chosen. Make no compliance claim here: the platform provides the mechanisms; the record of processing, the retention periods and the boundary of a remote GPU API are for the institution and its data protection officer to assess. If the Slim Dataprep uses a remote Docling, the document content crosses that boundary too.

30 / 43
Four layers: the instrumented services emit the signals, the Collector routes them, the Victoria components store the configured types, and Grafana presents the selected data sources. The deployment differences matter. Compose and Swarm include the Collector and the VictoriaLogs baseline; the full in-app OpenTelemetry, the trace and metrics stores and Grafana need their options. The Kubernetes chart enables the logs by default, while the metrics, the traces and Grafana have distinct opt-in settings and operator-managed components. The observability is configurable, so detailed traces cannot be promised before the deployed settings and the retention have been checked.

Deployment and operations

Choose the app platform and the GPU placement separately.

Application platform

Docker Compose runs the app stack on one host. Docker Swarm can orchestrate it across nodes. Kubernetes uses the GENIE.AI Helm chart.

Model-serving placement

Model services can run alongside the app environment on suitable GPU hosts or behind a dedicated external GPU API. All three platforms can use that API.

Hosting on premises or in the cloud is a separate decision.

Compose guide · Swarm guide · Kubernetes and Helm · Deployment topologies
33 / 43
Two choices that are often conflated. The application platform determines how the main services are packaged and operated; the model-serving placement determines where the GPU-backed endpoints run. "External" in the GPU setting means outside the application deployment — not the public internet, and not third-party hosting. The endpoint can stay inside the institution's own network. The constraints that shape each decision are the existing platform skills, the data boundaries and who owns the hardware.

Compose and Swarm use the dual-mode Compose configuration and can point to a dedicated node with GPU_NODE_HOST and the GPU API credential; they can also run local model services when the host and the scheduling support it. Kubernetes uses the Helm chart: the external mode takes the configured GPU host and the service paths, while the in-cluster mode uses the chart's GPU workload configuration and the documented NVIDIA device-plugin requirements. All three platforms support an external GPU API, and choosing that API does not dictate which application platform to use.

Each application platform calls the same API boundary, and behind it sit the model and the parsing workloads. The split lets the application environment call the compatible service paths on a dedicated GPU host: vLLM for the generation or the translation, TEI for the embeddings or the reranking, and a remote Docling when that option is configured. The operational dependency is explicit — the endpoint has to be secured, its capacity and its availability monitored, its credentials managed and its network paths tested. The diagrams show a placement pattern, not a claim that every service runs on one physical node.

The institution compares the model fit in its service languages, the response quality, the context length, the latency and the expected concurrency on the target hardware. What can you configure in GENIE.AI?

Service and access

Set the app’s branding and available UI languages. Manage documents and OKF grants in the admin tools, and configure sign-in and role mapping in Keycloak.

Retrieval and models

Tune chunk size and overlap, retrieval depth and optional reranking. Select generation and embedding models to suit the service.

Infrastructure and telemetry

Configure deployment through environment variables or Helm values. Choose where model endpoints run and which telemetry services to enable.

Change how documents are chunked, then re-ingest them and test a reference question.

Branding · UI locales · Access control · Ingestion pipeline · Installation guide · Kubernetes and Helm
37 / 43
The configuration runs across the framework, and the permit guide makes it concrete. A content owner changes the source; an administrator triggers the ingestion; the deployment team tunes the chunk size and overlap, the model endpoints, the retrieval depth, the locales, the identity integration and the telemetry. The settings that change the stored index content are not the same as the settings that change the runtime behaviour: a chunking change requires a re-ingestion and a retrieval check, while enabling a UI locale or the traces has a different impact. Most deployments adapt many values, so the practical task is to document the ownership, validate the changes and keep the resulting configuration reproducible.

A public service needs owners at every layer.

Business team

Owns the official sources and helps decide whether responses meet the service’s needs.

Application team

Owns configuration, release changes, evaluation and the way the framework integrates with its channels.

Platform team

Owns identity, runtime services, observability, backup, recovery and availability within the deployed environment.

The changed renewal rule shows the handoffs. The business owner maintains the authority of the content; the application team configures, integrates and evaluates the assistant; the platform team keeps the identity, the data services, the runtime, the backup and the availability working. These responsibilities have to be assigned, even where one team covers several layers in a smaller institution. The question to answer is which existing teams could own each part of a local deployment.

The budget follows the service design.

Prepare

Budget for source preparation, access design, integration, and evaluation on realistic questions.

Host

Size application services and data stores separately from model serving. Measure GPU capacity at the expected concurrency and context length.

Operate

Budget for the people who update the corpus, run the platform, investigate issues and repeat evaluations.

The framework code is Apache 2.0. Models, data and service operations have their own terms and costs.

Apache 2.0 licence · Model selection · Deployment topologies
39 / 43
The budget follows the design. It covers the source preparation, the integration, the access design, the evaluation, the platform hosting and the operating model. The model serving can be sized separately from the application tier, particularly where the GPU capacity is shared or centrally managed. The people who curate the knowledge and respond to the incidents belong in the budget, not only the compute and the storage. The framework licence is Apache 2.0; the costs and the terms of the models, the data and the services are separate, and there is no universal price.
